messages:
hannah: Morning — quick bootstrap head-scratcher on my first day. I ran the dotfiles ./bootstrap and it created ~/.zprofile but not ~/.zshrc. When I open iTerm non-login shells some of the PATH tweaks from dotfiles aren't applied and `asdf` shims don't seem to resolve. Also pnpm installs still go to /usr/local and require sudo. macOS corporate laptop (Intel). Any quick triage?

omar: welcome! :wave: We expect the bootstrap to handle both login and interactive shells but some people have older shells. On macOS Catalina+ zsh uses ~/.zprofile for login shells and ~/.zshrc for interactive. Check which file your terminal runs: in iTerm preferences check "Command" for the profile (Login shell vs default shell).

hannah: iTerm was set to "Login shell" so it sources zprofile — but my GUI apps open new windows as interactive non-login sometimes. The dotfiles repo's bootstrap symlinked ~/.zprofile (and a ~/.zshenv) but not ~/.zshrc.

bryce: simplest fix is to source one from the other. We usually have at the top of ~/.zprofile: `[[ -f ~/.zshrc ]] && source ~/.zshrc` and in ~/.zshenv keep minimal PATH exports. But more importantly add the `asdf.sh` lines near the top of whichever is sourced for interactive shells:```# asdf
. $(brew --prefix asdf)/libexec/asdf.sh
. $(brew --prefix asdf)/etc/profile.d/asdf.sh
export PATH="$HOME/.asdf/bin:$HOME/.asdf/shims:$PATH"``` That ensures shims appear before /usr/bin.

hannah: I added the source line and the asdf lines to ~/.zprofile and restarted iTerm. `which asdf` -> /opt/homebrew/bin/asdf, but `asdf current` still empty. `asdf list` shows plugins. How do I get python and node installed easily?

omar: run `cat .tool-versions` in the repo root to see pinned versions. If none, the project uses direnv and package.json. If pinned, run `asdf install` to install all versions from ~/.tool-versions. For single runtime you can do `asdf install python 3.10.12` or `asdf install nodejs 18.17.0`. If python install fails, likely missing brew libs — run `brew install openssl readline xz zlib` and set build flags before install:```export LDFLAGS="-L$(brew --prefix openssl)/lib"
export CPPFLAGS="-I$(brew --prefix openssl)/include"
asdf install python 3.10.12```

hannah: ran `asdf install` and python/node are now available. One lingering issue: pnpm still installed to /usr/local when I ran `npm i -g pnpm` earlier. `npm config get prefix` -> /usr/local. I don't want sudo installs.

bryce: set an npm prefix to your home and add it early in PATH. Steps:```mkdir -p "$HOME/.npm-global"
npm config set prefix "$HOME/.npm-global"
# add this to your zshrc/zprofile before other PATH changes
export NPM_PACKAGES="$HOME/.npm-global"
export PATH="$NPM_PACKAGES/bin:$HOME/.asdf/shims:$PATH"``` Then reinstall global packages without sudo.

hannah: did that and `which pnpm` -> /Users/hannah/.npm-global/bin/pnpm. Also ran `direnv allow` in the repo to load local tool versions. All green now, thanks! :raised_hands:

onboard-bot: Created INF-1210: "dotfiles: update bootstrap to ensure ~/.zshrc coverage + note PATH ordering for asdf and npm prefix" assigned to @bryce.

bryce: I'll add a tiny PR to the dotfiles README reminding people about zprofile vs zshrc and the npm prefix ordering. Happy first day!
